chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Madinah, 'Where are the graves of the martyrs?' He said: 'Is not the best of the martyrs among you? And He to whom my soul belongs, there are around him four thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, weeping for him until the Day of Judgment.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the angels weeping for the best of the martyrs according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Rib'i ibn Abdillah inquires about the burial sites of martyrs in Medina, prompting Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) to highlight the supreme status of Imam Husayn (a.s.). The Imam testifies that four thousand angels, described as disheveled and dusty, weep for him until the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the cosmic scale of his martyrdom and the continuous divine mourning for his sacrifice.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from ‘Abbās ibn Ma’rūf, from Ḥammād ibn ‘Isā, from Rib’i ibn ‘Abdillāh, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) in Madīnah, “Where are the graves of the martyrs (of Uḥud)?” Imam (a.s.) replied: Is not the best of the martyrs – referring to Ḥusain (a.s.) – (buried) near you?! I swear to He who has my life in His Hand that there are four thousand angels around the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) who are disheveled, covered with dust, and who cry over him (and will continue to do so) until the Day of Judgment.
